relationships.subject: Burning Mouth Syndrome
relationships.evidence_quote: Increased expression of TRPV1 and CB2, along with decreased CB1 expression, was reported in the tongue epithelial cells of BMS patients [40].

relationships.subject: Burning Mouth Syndrome
relationships.evidence_quote: TRPV1, NGF and P2X3‐positive fibres were significantly elevated in BMS patients, correlating with pain levels [46, 47].

relationships.subject: Burning Mouth Syndrome
relationships.evidence_quote: IENF was significantly reduced in BMS patients compared to controls in four studies [28, 38, 41, 46]; but remained unchanged in one [43].

key_findings: Across 14 case-control studies, BMS tissue shows reduced epithelial nerve fibre density and elevated TRPV1, NGF and P2X3 nociceptive markers, with altered CB1/CB2 expression.
Sodium channel mRNA (Nav1.7, Nav1.8, Nav1.9) did not differ between BMS and controls; evidence quality is very low with high risk of bias.
